reading.body:
Insurance for AI infrastructure is being priced from live telemetry, parametric triggers, and synthetic scenarios rather than historical claims, because the exposure has no claims history.

The mechanisms split into three groups. Direct measurement prices data centre risk with vision models and sensor analytics, adjusting premiums against live thermals, humidity, and load variation. Policy conditions require red teaming, governance audits, and third party safety ratings before cover is granted. Financial structures replace loss adjustment with parametric payouts on temperature or power thresholds, and limits that scale with GPU consumption and deployment footprint.

This matters for AI because the underlying asset is physical compute. Data centres are priced on thermal and power telemetry, and downtime payouts trigger automatically when those thresholds are crossed. Correlated accumulation modelling addresses the systemic risk that one foundational model serving millions of businesses produces a single catastrophic loss.

These mechanisms do not reveal whether they are cheaper or more widely adopted than traditional cover, nor any premium levels or loss experience. They also do not cover liability for model outputs, only property, cyber, errors and omissions, downtime, and accumulation risk.
